podcast.body: Released on January 29, 1977, this four-track EP was the first "fully independent British punk rock record." Howard Devoto borrowed money from his father to finance it, and the band financed and distributed it themselves on a label they formed. This radical "do it yourself" approach proved to everyone that independent recording was possible. "So for Trackey P called Spiral Scratch and it came out on January 29th, 1977."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This EP was the first punk record to be self-released, entirely by the Buzzcocks themselves, without any outside help. Released on January 29, 1977, it cost them 500 pounds to record and release it on their self-established label, New Hormones. It was a revelation to young musicians, proving that anyone could release a record on their own. "On January 29, 1977, they released an EP called Spiral Scratch. This was the first punk record to be self-released that did everything by themselves with no outside help."
